title: FLA import: bitmap library display names not decoded — CMediaBits Contents records are scanned for sounds only, every imported bitmap is renamed 'Bitmap N'
description: parseFla8Contents decodes CMedia* catalog records into the sounds table only: registerCMediaSoundObject (flash8-binary.ts:3557-3577) and the CMediaSound/CMediaBits discovery scan (:3975-4061) deliberately EXCLUDE the CMediaBits backref (cmBitsBackref is computed just to be excluded, :4042-4048), and Fla8ContentsInfo has no bitmaps map at all. So buildFla8Document names every imported bitmap 'Bitmap N' (flash8-import.ts:2035 createBitmap()) even though the genuine CMediaBits record carries the authored library display name as a BomString right after the 'Media N' stream name (same body shape as CMediaSound — see the writer's own byte-verified layout in write/contents-write.ts:217-268 and docs/21 sec 8.10). fixtures/evaporatingdrip.fla has a real CMediaBits ('Media 4') to verify against; Magnet.fla has many. Why it matters: library fidelity — a re-saved import renames the user's assets; also our own saveRealFla emits CMediaBits displayName=bmp.name, so a dash-authored doc's bitmap names survive one save but a REAL Flash FLA's don't, and a dash save->reopen keeps names only by accident of the same scan gap being symmetric (it isn't: reopen also yields 'Bitmap N'). Verify: saveRealFla a doc with a bitmap named 'Hero' then tryLoadRealFla — the item comes back 'Bitmap 1'. Fix: add a bitmaps map to Fla8ContentsInfo, register CMediaBits bodies (reuse registerCMediaSoundObject's shape; key by Media number), and use it in buildFla8Document for createBitmap's name (fall back to 'Bitmap N'). Consider also decoding the bitmap's AsLinkage (linkageIdentifier for attachBitmapData-era sharing) while there — optional. Acceptance: (a) round-trip test: bitmap library name survives saveRealFla->tryLoadRealFla; (b) fixture test: importing evaporatingdrip.fla yields the genuine authored display name for Media 4 instead of 'Bitmap 4'.
